# Browsing the package server in a browser

This page is for anyone who wants to see what is on the package server without a command line. It explains the
pages you get when you open the server in a browser, what each column means, and where to look when a page does not
tell you enough.

## Contents

1. [Where to start](#where-to-start)
2. [The listing pages](#the-listing-pages)
3. [What the columns mean](#what-the-columns-mean)
4. [Opening files](#opening-files)
5. [What the listing does not show](#what-the-listing-does-not-show)
6. [The same files on GitHub](#the-same-files-on-github)
7. [From the setup wizard](#from-the-setup-wizard)
8. [Related pages](#related-pages)

## Where to start

| Open | You see |
|---|---|
| <https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/> | the top level: `exponential/`, `CNAME`, `README.md`, `crossdomain.xml` |
| <https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/> | one folder per release, `6.0.0` to `6.0.15` |
| <https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/> | the packages of 6.0.15, `index.xml` and `thumbnails/` |
| <https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/thumbnails/> | the site package pictures |

Each address ends in `/`. Without it, the server answers with a redirect to the address with `/`.

## The listing pages

The pages titled "Index of /..." are not written by hand. A GitHub Actions workflow in the server's repository runs
the [github-pages-directory-listing](https://github.com/jayanta525/github-pages-directory-listing) action on every
push, which writes an `index.html` into each folder before GitHub Pages publishes it
([The package server on GitHub](the-package-server-on-github.md)).

A listing page has:

- the heading "Index of /exponential/6.0/6.0.15" (the path of the folder);
- a `../` row that leads one folder up;
- one row per folder first, then one row per file, each with an icon for its kind;
- a table with the columns **Name**, **Size** and **Last Modified**.

The page loads its styles from a public CDN, so it looks plain when the browser blocks outside scripts. The links
work either way.

## What the columns mean

| Column | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Name | the file or folder; a folder ends in `/` | `sevenx_multisite.ezpkg` |
| Size | the file size, in units of 1024 bytes labeled `KB` and `MB`; `-` for a folder | `89.16 KB` |
| Last Modified | the time the file was written by the deployment run, in UTC | `2026-10-16 20:42:40 UTC` |

> **Note**
> **Last Modified is the time of the last deployment, not of the last change to the file.** Every push rebuilds the
> whole site, so all files of the site show the same time. To see when a package really changed, look at its history
> on GitHub (below).

## Opening files

| File | What the browser does |
|---|---|
| `index.xml` | shows the XML (served as `application/xml`); the site packages are at the end ([The index.xml format](the-index-xml-format.md)) |
| `*.ezpkg` | downloads the archive (served as `application/octet-stream`) |
| `thumbnails/*.png` | shows the picture |
| `README.md` | shows or downloads the Markdown text, depending on the browser |

A downloaded `.ezpkg` is a gzip compressed tar archive. Most archive tools open it after you rename it to
`.tar.gz`; on the command line `tar -tzf` lists it as it is
([Downloading a package by hand](downloading-a-package-by-hand.md)).

## What the listing does not show

- **Hidden folders.** The top-level page lists `.git/` and `.github/`, but GitHub Pages does not serve folders that
  start with a dot: those links answer `404`. Read `.github/` on GitHub instead.
- **Versions and descriptions.** A listing knows file names and sizes only. The summary, version and type of each
  package are in `index.xml`.
- **Which packages an installation uses.** An installation reads one release folder, the one its
  `RemotePackagesIndexURL` names ([Package server settings](package-server-settings.md)).
- **History.** Earlier versions of a package are not kept on the site; a fix replaces the file in its release folder.
  Git keeps every earlier version.

## The same files on GitHub

The repository shows the same tree with history:

| You want | Open |
|---|---|
| the tree | <https://github.com/se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth> |
| the commits that changed one package | the file in the tree, then **History** |
| the deployments | the repository's [Actions](https://github.com/se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth/actions) tab |

Large files are not shown as text on GitHub; use **Download raw file**, or the package server address, to get them.
Each commit names the package it changed, for example "Updated: The cjw_multisite package's installer activates
ezownerchange".

## From the setup wizard

The **Site package** step of the setup wizard links to the server in two places
(`design/standard/templates/setup/init/site_types.tpl`):

- with an error, "Remote repository URL:" followed by the release folder it tried
  (`RemotePackagesIndexURL`);
- under **Additional packages**, "Full archive of all packages can be found here", which opens
  `RemotePackagesIndexURLBase`, by default <https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential>.
